title: How the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World Works, Part I
summary: Josh Clark and guest producer Noel open Part I of a two-part look at the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. They cover the origin of the list in ancient Greece (attributed to Diodorus of Sicily, with the "theamata" tourist idea), and the list's shifting membership. The episode then covers the Great Pyramid of Giza (Khufu's pyramid: size, construction, unfinished theories, earthquakes, and the modern Pizza Hut and KFC near it), the Hanging Gardens of Babylon (legend, lack of evidence, possible Nineveh location), and the Temple of Artemis at Ephesus (construction, the Artemis/Cybele statue, Antipater of Sidon's praise, Herostratus's arson, and later destruction). The episode ends with a tease for Part II and listener contact information. Opening banter includes tour dates for San Francisco Sketch Fest.
topics: Seven Wonders of the Ancient World

segments.title: Opening banter and tour dates
segments.summary: Hosts promote San Francisco Sketch Fest and Seattle and Portland tour dates, then introduce the two-part Seven Wonders episode with guest producer Noel.

segments.title: Overview of the Seven Wonders list
segments.summary: The hosts name the seven wonders in chronological order and explain the list's origin in ancient Greece, attributed to Diodorus of Sicily. Greek wealth and leisure made tourism possible, and the theamata were things to be seen. The list changed over time, including the removal of the Walls of Babylon.
topics: Seven Wonders of the Ancient World

segments.title: Ruins, travel, and Pizza Hut near the pyramids
segments.summary: The hosts discuss visiting ancient ruins such as Pompeii and Rome's Colosseum, then the Pizza Hut and KFC restaurants visible near the Great Pyramids.

segments.title: Great Pyramid of Giza: size and construction
segments.summary: The Great Pyramid of Khufu is the only surviving wonder. The hosts cover its height, its time as the tallest human-made structure until Lincoln Cathedral, its roughly 2 million blocks, its alignment to the cardinal directions, and its original limestone casing.

segments.title: Unfinished pyramid theories and hidden chambers
segments.summary: The hosts discuss evidence the pyramid may have been unfinished, including missing inscriptions and an unused sarcophagus. Other theories are that it was looted or that its passages are decoys. They also cover Abdullah al-Mamun's ninth-century tunnel as the modern entrance.

segments.title: Hanging Gardens of Babylon
segments.summary: The hosts describe the legendary Hanging Gardens, said to be built by Nebuchadnezzar for his wife Amytis. They note the lack of evidence, the absence of mention in Nebuchadnezzar's inscriptions and in Herodotus, and the theory that they stood in Nineveh, where irrigation structures have been found.

segments.title: Temple of Artemis at Ephesus: construction and statue
segments.summary: The hosts describe the city of Ephesus, the temple's construction under Croesus, its columns and dimensions, and the statue of Artemis with its many bulb-like objects. They discuss the cult of Cybele and the debate over whether these are breasts or bull testicles.

segments.title: Herostratus arson, rebuilding, and destruction
segments.summary: Herostratus burned the temple on the night Alexander the Great was born. The hosts discuss the decree against his name, Alexander's alleged offer to fund a rebuild, and the Goth destruction in 262. They mention a later Christian destruction, and Antipater of Sidon's praise of the temple.

segments.title: Closing and listener contact
segments.summary: The hosts preview Part II and give social media, email, and website details.
